title: Clyde Hart and Freddie Webster: the breathing marks arrangement
summary: Clyde Hart's arrangement of A Sinner Kissed an Angel, with Freddie Webster teaching the band to breathe together.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Oh, 1940-42. Uh huh. Any interesting things you'd like to talk about in the band? I mean, during your travels and things like that?

Well, after Bill Dogett left, we got Clyde Hart in the band -- Clyde Hart was playing piano with us and arranging. And I think Archie Johnson left, and then we got Freddie Webster in his place; he was a great trumpet player, Freddie Webster.

And I'll never forget this arrangement that Clyde Hart wrote on "A Sinner Kissed an Angel", and how Freddie Webster was letting everybody in the band know how to breathe, and in fact, he came to rehearsal with a pocket full of pencils

so that everybody could mark where they were supposed to breathe at -- it was one of the most wonderful things you'd ever want to hear; in fact, I wish we had made a recording of that arrangement, because it was so great to hear the band, the ensemble, the way it was played, you know? It sounded like it was just one person playing the whole thing.
It was real precision in the band, then?
